text: Sugar ' X ' A. is found in honey. B. is a keto sugar. C. exists in αα and ββ - anomeric forms. D. is laevorotatory. ' X ' is
explanation: Sugar 'X' Properties and Identification Sugars are classified based on their chemical structure, optical activity, and functional groups.Anomers (α- and &beta-) are forms of sugars that differ in the configuration at the anomeric carbon.Keto sugars contain a ketone group, whereas aldo sugars contain an aldehyde group. A: Sugar 'X' is found in honey. This points to fructose, which is a major sugar in honey.B: Sugar 'X' is a keto sugar. Fructose has a ketone functional group, confirming it is a keto sugar.C: Sugar 'X' exists in α and β anomeric forms. Fructose exhibits these forms due to the configuration at its anomeric carbon.D: Sugar 'X' is laevorotatory. Fructose is known to rotate plane-polarized light to the left, making it laevorotatory.Thus, the sugar 'X' is D-Fructose.

text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Glycogen is similar to amylose in its structure. Statement II: Glycogen is found in yeast and fungi also

options.A: Statement I is correct and Statement II is incorrect.
options.B: Statement I is incorrect and Statement II is correct.
options.C: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
options.D: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

explanation: Statement I: Glycogen is similar to amylose in its structure. Incorrect: While both glycogen and amylose are polysaccharides, their structures are different. Amylose is a linear polymer of glucose, while glycogen is a branched polymer of glucose with more frequent branching points. So, glycogen is not similar to amylose in structure. Statement II: Glycogen is found in yeast and fungi also. Correct: Glycogen is indeed found in yeast, fungi, and other organisms as a form of energy storage, similar to how it is found in animals. Thus, the correct answer is (b): Statement I is incorrect and Statement II is correct.

text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: A unit formed by the attachment of a base to 1' position of sugar is known as nucleoside. Statement II: When nucleoside is linked to phosphorous acid at 5' -position of sugar moiety, we get nucleotide

options.A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
options.B: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
options.C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
options.D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true

explanation: When nucleoside is linked to phosphoric acid at 5' position of sugar moiety we get a nucleotide Statement II is incorrect because not link with phosphorous acid. Statement I: Correct. A nucleoside is formed by the attachment of a nitrogenous base to the 1' position of a sugar (ribose or deoxyribose) via a glycosidic bond.Statement II: Incorrect. A nucleotide is formed when a nucleoside is linked to phosphoric acid (H₃PO₄), not phosphorous acid (H₃PO₃), at the 5' position of the sugar moiety. Phosphoric acid is a key component in the structure of nucleotides, which are the building blocks of DNA and RNA. Conclusion: The correct answer is (c) Statement I is true, and Statement II is false.
